sources.note: Data format (IEEE 754 float in two registers, counters as 32-bit or 64-bit integers) and the bytes/words swap register

notes: Electrex Femto energy analyzer (Femto 96 and Femto D4).

Modbus RTU slave on RS-485. Factory settings of the meter: address 27, 38400 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 2 stop bits; the address (1 to 247), rate (2400 to 38400), data bits (7 or 8), parity and stop bits (1 or 2) are set in the RS485 menu.

Addresses are the register numbers printed in the manual (200 is the first); they are written here as printed, address base 0. Each measurement is a single-precision IEEE 754 float in two consecutive registers (the table lists every second address).

Big-endian byte and word order, the default: the most significant word is in the lower register (the manual's example reads U1N 230.753 V as 0x4366 at 220 and 0xC0C4 at 221). It changes if the bytes/words swap register is programmed.

The manual's table is the list of registers that can be chosen for the alarms; it is the only register list in the installation instructions. It gives no function code, only 'input register', so they are listed as input registers.
Which values are valid depends on the wiring selected on the meter (3P4W, 3P3W, single-phase and so on). Power and power-factor registers are signed (import/export).
The two external pulse counter registers (376 and 384) are in the manual's table but are left out: counters are 32-bit or 64-bit integers and the manual does not say which for these.
The bytes/words swap register is a holding register at address 216 for the Femto family; its default is 0 (big endian), which is the order used here.
Written from the manufacturer's manual; not tested on a device.

registers.description: 0 = big endian (default). Bit 0 and 8 swap bytes, bit 1 and 9 swap words, bit 2 and 10 swap double words, bit 3 and 11 swap float words, bit 4 and 12 swap float bytes; the high and low byte written must be equal (for example 0x0303).
